user.title: Describe your house
user.description: Three answers are enough to start. You can change everything later.

data_description.name: Shown as the device name, e.g. "Home" or "Granny flat".
data_description.heating_type: What heats this house. It decides how calmly Thermogeist regulates.
data_description.outdoor_temperature_entity: An outdoor thermometer in the shade, the heat pump's outdoor sensor, or your weather entity (e.g. Forecast Home). Several thermometers? Combine them with the helper "Combine the state of several sensors", type minimum – one is always in the shade.

details.title: A few questions
details.description: Your answers decide what Thermogeist asks next. Everything can be changed later.

data.heat_load_known: Do you know the heat load?

data_description.heat_load_known: Yes, if you have a heat load calculation (heating installer or energy consultant).
data_description.flow_measurement: A sensor for the water going to the radiators (flow) and, optionally, coming back (return). Without a sensor, the heating curve set on your heat pump or boiler is the next best thing.
data_description.living_area: Total heated floor area of the house, without balconies and terraces. Thermogeist uses it to estimate each room's share of the heat load from the room's size, e.g. 20 m² of 160 m² ≈ 12.5 %.

heat_load.title: Heat load
heat_load.description: Values from your heat load calculation.

data_description.heat_load: Heat the house needs on the coldest design day, from your heat load calculation (heating installer or energy consultant). Leave empty if unknown.
data_description.design_outdoor_temperature: The outdoor temperature your heat load was calculated for. Required if you enter a heat load. Not sure? Search the web for "design outdoor temperature" (in Germany: "Normaußentemperatur") together with your postcode.
data_description.share_outside: Part of the heat load in rooms Thermogeist does not control, e.g. a bathroom with floor heating. Only needed if you know it from a heat load calculation; otherwise Thermogeist works it out from the living area. Leave empty for 0 %.

flow.title: Water temperatures
flow.description: The sensors in the heating circuit.

data_description.flow_temperature_entity: Optional. The temperature of the water going to the radiators. Best: a sensor in the heating circuit (after a buffer tank, if you have one). Avoid the heat pump's own flow sensor: during hot-water charging it shows 45–50 °C and Thermogeist would close the valves although the radiators get cooler. Strap-on sensors often read 2–4 K too low – calibrate them. See the docs: Thermostats → Choosing the flow temperature sensor.
data_description.return_temperature_entity: Optional. The temperature of the water coming back from the radiators, measured at the same place as the flow (e.g. heating circuit return). Thermogeist then uses the measured difference between flow and return instead of assuming 5 K. Calibrate strap-on sensors the same way as the flow sensor.

heating_curve.title: Heating curve
heating_curve.description: Two points of the heating curve set on your heat pump or boiler – you find them in its menu or app, often as a chart. Thermogeist draws a straight line between them and uses it as the flow temperature.

data.curve_cold_flow: Flow temperature when it is cold
data.curve_warm_flow: Flow temperature when it is mild

data_description.curve_cold_outdoor: A cold day, e.g. −10 °C. Best: the coldest point of your curve.
data_description.curve_cold_flow: The flow temperature your heating sets at that outdoor temperature, e.g. 45 °C.
data_description.curve_warm_outdoor: A mild day, e.g. 15 °C. Best: the warmest point of your curve.
data_description.curve_warm_flow: The flow temperature at that outdoor temperature, e.g. 30 °C. Colder and warmer than the two points, Thermogeist keeps their values, like the heating does.

error.design_temperature_required: A heat load needs the design outdoor temperature it was calculated for.
error.heat_load_out_of_range: Heat load must be between 0.5 and 100 kW.
error.design_outdoor_temperature_out_of_range: Design outdoor temperature must be between −40 and +10 °C.
error.living_area_out_of_range: Living area must be between 10 and 10,000 m².
error.curve_warm_not_above_cold: The mild outdoor temperature must be warmer than the cold one.
error.curve_flow_rises_when_warmer: When it is mild, the flow must not be warmer than when it is cold – are the two points swapped?

init.title: House settings
init.description: Change your house description. Thermogeist reloads afterwards.

user.title: Add a room
user.description: Which room, which temperature sensor, and how should Thermogeist get its share of the heat load?

data_description.name: Shown as the device name, e.g. "Living room".
data_description.area: Optional. The room device is placed in this Home Assistant area.
data_description.temperature_entity: A sensor in the room, ideally away from the radiator and out of direct sunlight.
data_description.share_mode: Most people let Thermogeist estimate it. If you have a room-by-room heat load calculation, enter the value instead.

windows_devices.name: Windows and devices
windows_devices.description: Optional: contacts that pause heating, and devices whose heat counts.

data_description.window_sensors: Optional. If any of them is open for 30 seconds, the room stops heating until it is closed again.
data_description.heat_sources: Optional. Power sensors (W) of devices in this room, e.g. a PC, server or fridge. Their heat is subtracted from what the radiator has to deliver. Next you say how much of each device's power stays in the room.

data_description.design_indoor_temperature: Planning value from the heat load calculation, not the temperature you heat to. Usually 20 °C; bathrooms 24 °C, heated halls 15 °C. Your setpoint decides how warm the room really gets.

geometry.title: Size and position
geometry.description: Rough values are fine. Learning will correct the estimate later.

data_description.floor_area: Galleries and open spaces count their floor area once.
data_description.ceiling_height: With a sloped ceiling: the highest point.
data_description.exterior_walls: Walls that face outside. A corner room usually has 2, a hallway inside the house 0.
data_description.above: What is directly above the ceiling.
data_description.below: What is directly below the floor.

sloped_ceiling.name: Sloped ceiling
sloped_ceiling.description: Only for rooms under a sloped roof.

data.ceiling_low: Lowest point under a sloped ceiling

data_description.ceiling_low: Only for sloped ceilings. Thermogeist uses the mean of lowest and highest point.

known_share.title: Known share
known_share.description: Enter the room's share of the house heat load from your heat load calculation.

data_description.known_share: Room heat load divided by house heat load, in percent.

heat_source_factors.title: How much heat stays in the room?
heat_source_factors.description: Per device: the share of its power that stays in the room as heat ({devices}). 100 % for electronics, lights, fridges and heat pump dryers. Less for devices whose heat leaves with exhaust air or waste water, e.g. vented dryer 10–20 %, washing machine 10–20 %, dishwasher 20–40 %. More for an air conditioner heating the room: its COP × 100 %, e.g. 400 % (choose a little below the SCOP on the energy label). Optional per device: a factor sensor in % (e.g. a template) that wins over the number while it is available. See the docs: Rooms → Devices that heat the room.

factor_sensors.name: Factor from a sensor
factor_sensors.description: Optional: a sensor in % per device, e.g. a COP template for an air conditioner.

edit_room.description: Which room, which temperature sensor, and how should Thermogeist get its share of the heat load?

reconfigure.title: Change room
reconfigure.description: What would you like to change?

thermostat.title: Thermostat
thermostat.description: Choose the thermostat device. Thermogeist recognises known models and fills in the rest.

data_description.device: The thermostat device in Home Assistant (it must have a climate entity).
data_description.rated_output: Optional. The radiator's output in W at 75/65/20 °C from its data sheet or type plate. Enables the feed-forward and, later, sizing diagnostics.

roles.title: What does what?
roles.description: Detected profile: {profile}. Check the entities below; empty fields are simply not used. {notes}

data_description.climate: The thermostat's own climate entity (setpoint, its temperature).
data_description.valve_read: Only if the thermostat reports how far its valve really is open. Leave empty for Sonoff thermostats; never the entity from valve position (set).
data_description.valve_write: Lets Thermogeist set the valve position directly. Without it the thermostat is controlled by setpoint.
data_description.valve_min: A fallback stored on the device; it still works when Home Assistant is down.
data_description.external_temperature: Lets the thermostat use the room sensor instead of its own.
data_description.strategy: Automatic: by valve position if the thermostat allows it, otherwise by setpoint. Valve: Thermogeist sets the valve itself (calm, with minimum opening). Setpoint: Thermogeist tells the thermostat which temperature to aim for, and the thermostat moves its valve itself.

detected_roles.name: Detected roles – check if you like
detected_roles.description: Thermogeist found these entities. Open only to change them.

data_description.climate: The thermostat's own climate entity (setpoint, its temperature).
data_description.valve_read: Only if the thermostat reports how far its valve really is open. Leave empty for Sonoff thermostats; never the entity from valve position (set).
data_description.valve_write: Lets Thermogeist set the valve position directly. Without it the thermostat is controlled by setpoint.
data_description.valve_min: A fallback stored on the device; it still works when Home Assistant is down.
data_description.external_temperature: Lets the thermostat use the room sensor instead of its own.

more.name: More
more.description: Calibration and valve confirmation; rarely changed.

data_description.valve_refresh_minutes: Some thermostats drop a valve position set from outside after a while (Bosch: after 15 minutes). Thermogeist then resends the unchanged value at this interval – a radio message, no motor movement. Empty = off.

remove_thermostat.title: Remove thermostat
remove_thermostat.description: The thermostat gets its own device settings back and regulates on its own again.

new_room_thermostats.title: Thermostats and heaters of {room}
new_room_thermostats.description: Add the thermostats or heaters of this room now ({count} so far), or finish. A room has either thermostats or heaters.

heater.title: Heater
heater.description: A heater that Thermogeist switches instead of moving a valve, e.g. a smart plug in front of a fan convector or an infrared panel. Thermogeist does not know your device: if it has several stages, a template sensor tells which stage runs, and optionally a template number sets it.

data_description.switch: Switches the heater on and off.
data_description.energy_source: Heating circuit: the heat comes from the heating water (plinth heater, fan convector), its output depends on the flow temperature. Electric: the heat is made by electricity (infrared, fan heater) and does not depend on the flow temperature.
data_description.stage_outputs: One value per stage, from low to high, separated by commas, e.g. "1300, 1700". Heating circuit: the rated output at 75/65/20 °C from the data sheet. Electric: the output itself. Not the power the fan draws.

more.name: Stages and details
more.description: Template entities for heaters with several stages, and details for an exact output.

data_description.stage_sensor: An entity whose state is the running stage: 0 = not running, 1, 2 … Typically a template sensor, e.g. from the power of a smart plug. Also reports a heater that is switched on but does not run.
data_description.stage_setter: A number entity that takes the stage 1, 2 … – typically a template number that switches your device. Without it Thermogeist only switches on and off, and the heater keeps its own stage.
data_description.off_output: Heat the heater still gives while switched off, e.g. heating water flowing through a plinth heater with the fan off. From the data sheet; usually 0.
data_description.exponent: Only for the heating circuit. Radiators 1.3 (default), fan convectors about 1.0 – see the data sheet.

error.floor_area_out_of_range: Floor area must be between 1 and 500 m².
error.ceiling_height_out_of_range: Ceiling height must be between 1 and 12 m.
error.ceiling_low_out_of_range: The lowest point must be between 1 and 12 m.
error.ceiling_low_above_height: The lowest point cannot be higher than the ceiling height.
error.exterior_walls_out_of_range: Exterior walls must be between 0 and 4.
error.known_share_out_of_range: The share must be between 0 and 100 %.
error.known_shares_exceed_total: Together with the other rooms and the share outside Thermogeist this is more than 100 %.
error.design_indoor_temperature_out_of_range: Design indoor temperature must be between 10 and 30 °C.
error.role_needs_percent: This entity does not report a percentage. Choose the valve position entity (unit %).
error.role_needs_temperature: This entity is not a temperature input.
error.valve_strategy_needs_valve_write: The strategy “by valve position” needs the entity “Valve position (set)”. Choose it or pick another strategy.
error.valve_read_is_write: This is the entity Thermogeist writes to; it only shows what Thermogeist set, not where the valve is. Leave the field empty if the thermostat does not report its valve position.
error.heater_outputs_count: Enter exactly one output per stage.
error.heater_outputs_rising: The outputs must rise from stage to stage, and the output while off must be below the first stage.
error.heater_outputs_unreadable: Enter numbers separated by commas, e.g. "1300, 1700".
error.heater_needs_stage_entity: With more than one stage Thermogeist needs to know which one runs: choose a stage sensor or a stage setter.

abort.room_has_thermostats: This room already has thermostats. A room has either thermostats or heaters; remove the thermostats first.
abort.room_has_heaters: This room already has heaters. A room has either thermostats or heaters; remove the heaters first.

no_thermostat.message: This room has no thermostat yet. Add a thermostat to the room first.

logbook_manual_setpoint.message: set to {setpoint} °C on {thermostat}; new room setpoint

logbook_learned_demand.message: needs about {percent} % of the heat its inputs suggest (learned)

logbook_device_overrides_valve.message: {thermostat} keeps changing its valve position on its own; room switched back to observe

logbook_frost_guard.message: window open, but the room fell below {setpoint} °C: heating to frost protection

child_lock_off.message: The child lock of this room is off. Switch it on first.

logbook_child_lock_adopted.message: Child lock switched on at {thermostat}; it now stays on for the whole room

logbook_child_lock_reset.message: Child lock of {thermostat} had gone off; switched on again

logbook_child_lock_pause_ended.message: Child lock switched on again at {thermostat}; the 30 minutes are over early

logbook_not_calibrated.message: {thermostat} is not calibrated; its valve probably stays fully open

logbook_heater_not_running.message: {heater} is switched on but does not run

sensor_stale.title: Room temperature sensor of {room} is silent
sensor_stale.description: The sensor {sensor} is unavailable or has not reported a new value for a long time. Thermogeist keeps the valve at its minimum opening until it reports again. Check its battery and connection.

device_overrides_valve.title: {thermostat} keeps regulating on its own
device_overrides_valve.description: Thermogeist wrote the valve position of {thermostat} several times, but the thermostat changed it back each time. Control for {room} was switched off; the thermostat regulates on its own again. See the FAQ for what to check, then switch control on again.

radiator_undersized.title: Radiators in {room} are probably too small
radiator_undersized.description: On the coldest design day {room} will probably not reach its setpoint: its radiators deliver less heat at the learned flow temperature than the room loses. The sensor Radiator size shows the numbers and the probable cause. See the FAQ for what you can do.

radiator_oversized.title: Radiators in {room} are much larger than needed
radiator_oversized.description: Even on the coldest design day {room} needs less than a third of what its radiators can deliver. The valve works mostly almost closed, which makes control less fine. See the FAQ for what you can do.

flow_higher_than_needed.title: Flow temperature of {house} is probably higher than needed
flow_higher_than_needed.description: All rooms of {house} need less than a third of what their radiators deliver, even on the coldest design day. A lower heating curve would probably be enough and saves energy, especially with a heat pump. Thermogeist does not change the heating system; see the FAQ.

thermostat_not_calibrated.title: {thermostat} is not calibrated
thermostat_not_calibrated.description: {thermostat} in {room} reports that it lost its calibration, e.g. after a firmware update. It no longer moves its valve, which usually stays fully open in the mounting position. Thermogeist shows its valve position as unknown. Recalibrate the thermostat (Sonoff: press the button briefly; with child lock on, first use *Child lock: off for 30 min*). The issue disappears by itself once the thermostat is calibrated again.

heater_not_running.title: {heater} does not run
heater_not_running.description: {heater} in {room} is switched on, but its stage sensor says it does not run. Check the fuse, the device and the template of the stage sensor. While this lasts Thermogeist counts no heat from {heater}.
